refuters.argument:
Row CV:def:interlace, bundle CV.InterlaceData (reviewer input lines 274-315), theorem CV.interlace_definition (line 318), binder hP : CrossingGeometry P. I expanded every field to primitives (SM.IsCrossing/Crossing = remote pair whose closed segments meet; crossingPoint; CrossingGeometry = nonzero edges, remote closed segments meet only at interior transverse points, no three edge interiors concur; geometricVisitPosition v = (edge of v, crossing parameter in (0,1)); traversalBetween = strict cyclic betweenness on key i.val + t; GeometricInterlaces = x ≠ y and alternating visits; CV.Diagrammatic and CV.selfIntersections from Setup.lean) and then tried to build a polygon on which a bundle clause and the printed clause (d1_setup.tex 346-353 with the preamble 303-313) disagree. None exists; details:

(1) DOMAIN. The printed row is for a diagrammatic polygon; the bundle is stated for CrossingGeometry P. diagrammatic_iff (Setup.lean 1630) says Diagrammatic <-> CrossingGeometry AND no vertex on a non-incident segment. Hand check: if P i ∈ edgeSegment P e with e ∉ {i-1, i}, then either e is remote to edge i (closed segments of e_i and e share p_i, and CrossingGeometry forces p_i ∈ edgeInterior P i, impossible since p_i = edgePoint i 0 with d_i ≠ 0), or e = i+1, and then for every n ≥ 4 the edges e_{i-1}, e_{i+1} are remote and share p_i = edgePoint (i-1) 1, again not interior. Hence for n ≥ 4 CrossingGeometry ⟹ Diagrammatic: the Lean binder IS the printed class. For n ≤ 3 there are no remote pairs (adjacent i j := j-i ∈ {-1,0,1} covers ZMod 3), so Crossing P = ∅ for every P and all graph clauses concern the empty graph. The only extra polygons admitted by the Lean are non-diagrammatic n=3 tuples such as p0=(0,0), p1=(-1,0), p2=(1,0) (CrossingGeometry holds vacuously; p0 lies inside the non-incident e1; selfIntersections = {(0,0)} while Crossing P = ∅). On such a tuple the printed row says nothing, and the two bundle fields that mention double points (vertices 281-282, vertex_ncard 284-285) are guarded by Diagrammatic P and 3 ≤ n, so no clause is asserted about its double points. This is a harmless extension, not an object counted in/out differently. (Also n ∈ {1,2}: Crossing P empty, printed undefined.)

(2) VERTEX SET [m]. For a printed-diagrammatic P with n ≥ 3 I verified by hand that double points (points with two distinct preimages (i,s),(j,t), s,t ∈ [0,1)) are exactly the points of remote pairs whose closed segments meet: i = j is impossible (d_i ≠ 0); adjacent i,j meeting off the shared corner means the edges double back, putting p_i or p_{i+2} on a non-incident edge (excluded); the corner itself has only the preimage (i+1,0) since (i,1) is not a traversal parameter; conversely a remote pair meeting at a corner is a vertex on a non-incident (remote) edge (excluded), so the meeting point is interior to both, transverse, with exactly two preimages. Hence crossingPoint is a bijection Crossing P → selfIntersections P and m = Fintype.card (Crossing P), exactly the fields vertices/vertex_ncard. vertex_count (276) is the tautology card = crossingSet.card.

(3) ADJACENCY, concrete polygons. (a) Non-interlaced pair, Gauss word AABB: n = 7, p0=(0,0), p1=(4,0), p2=(4,2), p3=(2,-1), p4=(-2,-1), p5=(-2,-3), p6=(-1,1). All 14 remote pairs checked: exactly two crossings A={0,2} at (8/3,0) (params 2/3 on e0, 2/3 on e2) and B={3,5} at (-3/2,-1) (params 7/8 on e3, 1/2 on e5); no vertex on a non-incident edge; so P is diagrammatic, m = 2, and the two double points are the two crossing points (vertices field holds). Keys: A at 0.667 and 2.667; B at 3.875 and 5.5. traversalBetween(0.667, 3.875, 2.667): 0.667<3.875<2.667 false; 3.875<2.667 false; 2.667<0.667 false -> false; likewise for 5.5. So no visit of B lies between the two visits of A -> ¬GeometricInterlaces hP A B (exactly_one_between 298-301: zero, not exactly one). Printed: reading AABB, neither occurrence of B lies between the two A's -> not adjacent. Agree. Ind = {∅, {A}, {B}, {A,B}}, N({A}) = ∅ in both. (b) Interlaced pair: regular pentagram, n = 5, p_k at angle 144°k. Along e0 from p0 the crossing with e2 sits at s ≈ 0.382 and with e3 at s ≈ 0.618, so the Gauss word from p0 is ABCDEABCDE with A={0,2}, B={0,3}, C={1,3}, D={1,4}, E={2,4}. Keys: A at 0.382 and 2.618; B at 0.618 and 3.382. traversalBetween(0.382, 0.618, 2.618) true; traversalBetween(0.382, 3.382, 2.618) false in all three disjuncts -> exactly one -> GeometricInterlaces A B. Printed: exactly one B between the two A's -> adjacent. Agree (graph K5 in both). The equivalence is general: y has exactly two visits at positions distinct from x's (geometricVisitPosition_injective), the arcs x0->x1 and x1->x0 are complementary for them, so 'exactly one on one arc' <-> 'one on each arc' <-> the alternating-visit definition, for either order of x0,x1 (the field quantifies over both orders). The wrap across the cut at p0 (= printed p1) is covered by the three disjuncts of traversalBetween, and no visit sits on a corner (parameters in (0,1)).

(4) Remaining clauses. occurrences (289-292): two visits per crossing (card of the two-element Finset), every visit in geometricGaussList (sorted by key), length 2m, each visit evaluates to its crossing point — the preamble 306-313. adj (294) is rfl. symm (303) = '(The relation is symmetric.)'. irrefl (305): with c' = c neither occurrence of c lies strictly between the two occurrences of c, so not 'exactly one' — agrees with printed. mem_Ind/mem_Ind_iff/empty_mem_Ind (307-312) render Ind(G_P) including ∅; mem_N (314-315) renders N_{G_P}(S) as vertices adjacent to some element of S (for arbitrary S, as printed). CV.U/mem_U/U_eq_generic (177-218) and interlace_generic_agree (323-329) are ordinary theorems outside the structure InterlaceData, as the second-round brief requires.

Conclusion: no polygon, event or set was found on which any InterlaceData field and the printed definition disagree; found_counterexample = false. The only Lean-only behaviour is the vacuous coverage of non-diagrammatic n ≤ 3 tuples (and n ∈ {1,2}), where the printed row is undefined and the bundle asserts nothing about double points. ||
